extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, examiners and IP practitioners in Malaysia
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for preparing, filing and prosecuting patent (and utility innovation) applications in Malaysia, including patentability criteria, non‑patentable subject matter, required forms, timelines and examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Invention' [Sec. 12]
rubrics_metrics.description: "An idea of an inventor which permits in practice the solution to a specific problem in the field of technology"; an invention may be or may relate to a product or process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invention must enable a practical solution to a specific technical problem; treat product and process equally as possible inventions when drafting claims and description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty [Section 14]
rubrics_metrics.description: “An invention is new if it is not anticipated by prior art.” Prior art is defined as everything disclosed to the public, anywhere in the world, before the date of filing/priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art includes written description, oral description, by use or in any other way. Use feature analysis (compare claimed features against prior art items) to assess novelty. Novelty requires that no single prior art disclose all claim features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step [Section 15]
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the prior art, it would not have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider common general knowledge and combining of prior arts. Use feature tables to compare claimed features to multiple prior references. Examples show a claim can be novel but lack inventive step if an obvious material choice (e.g., aluminium as a 'lightweight material') would be apparent to skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Applicability [Section 16]
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is industrially applicable if it can be made or used in any kind of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure specification discloses practical modes of making or using the invention so it is clearly applicable to industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Patentable: Discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Discoveries are not patentable under Section 13(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mere discoveries of natural phenomena from technical applications or processes that implement those discoveries (applications may be patentable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Patentable: Scientific Theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific theories are not patentable under Section 13(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theory as such is excluded; practical technical implementations or inventions based on a theory may be patentable if they meet other criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Patentable: Mathematical Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical methods are not patentable under Section 13(c) as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application of a mathematical method to produce a technical effect (e.g., a calculating machine or an image processing method that operates on image-representative numbers) can be patentable — draft claims to emphasize technical application rather than pure algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Patentable: Plant and Animal Varieties / Essentially Biological Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant and animal varieties or essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals are not patentable, except man‑made living micro‑organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biotech filings should focus on man‑made microorganisms or technical processes that fall outside 'essentially biological' exclusions where possible; consider alternative claim drafting strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Patentable: Schemes, Rules or Methods for Doing Business, Mental Acts, or Playing Games
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemes, rules or methods for doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games are not patentable under Section 13(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims framed as abstract business methods or pure game rules will be excluded; where a technical implementation exists, draft claims emphasizing technical steps or apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Patentable: Methods for Treatment and Diagnostic Methods Practiced on the Human or Animal Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for treatment of human or animal body by surgery or therapy, and diagnostic methods practiced on the human or animal body, are not patentable under Section 13(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical procedure claims directed to surgical/therapeutic or diagnostic methods are excluded; consider claiming medical devices, compositions or in vitro methods where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions (unity of invention requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims for single inventive concept; multiple unrelated inventions should be filed in separate applications or subject to divisional filings. Use claim dependency and common inventive concept to defend unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Patent Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent specification should include Drawings, Abstract, Claim(s), and Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each section is complete: claims define scope, description supports and enables claims, drawings illustrate embodiments, and abstract summarises invention for publication. Thoroughly read and understand the specification before filing or prosecuting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Requirements and Initial Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application filing at MyIPO requires Form 1 (RM290) / Form 14 (RM140) - required; Form 17 (RM80); Form 22 (RM80); Patent Specification in English or national language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare required forms and fees at filing. Ensure specification language and required bibliographic data are correct to avoid formal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Filing via MyIPO as Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: When using MyIPO as Receiving Office submit Form PCT/RO/101 and a patent specification in English; pay transmittal fees, international filing fee and search fee; select an ISA (KIPO/JPO/IPAustralia/EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for transmittal (~RM550), international filing (~RM6110) and search fees (RM5940–RM9237). Choose ISA strategically based on search quality and expected costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Examination: Types and Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests include Substantive Examination (Form 5), Modified Substantive Examination (Form 5A) and Deferment (Form 5B); expedited procedures via Form 5H/SD and subsequent Form 5I upon approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand fee differentials (e.g., Form 5 RM1100 manual, Form 5A RM640 manual, expedited Form 5H/SD RM250 and Form 5I RM2200). Use modified examination when relying on corresponding granted patents from prescribed countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified Examination Requirements and Prescribed Countries
rubrics_metrics.description: For modified examination (Form 5A) submit prescribed fees and a certified true copy of the patent granted to the applicant in a prescribed country or Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed countries/conventions include Australia, Japan, Republic of Korea, United Kingdom, United States of America and the European Patent Convention. Ensure certified copies are in the prescribed form to qualify for modified exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines: Public Inspection and Time Limit for Requesting Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Application is available for public inspection 18 months after the priority date/filing date; timelines for requesting examination are shown (timeline indicates up to 5 years for requesting substantive examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor 18‑month publication and ensure Form 5/5A/5B is filed within statutory windows (commonly within 5 years from filing/priority for substantive exam) to avoid losing examination rights; use Form 5B to defer if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Searching Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to search: free patent databases, MyIPO internal database (MyIPO IP Online), subscribed databases such as Epoquenet, GPI & STN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct comprehensive searches across multiple databases before filing to assess novelty and inventive step; document search strategies and references for prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty Test: Feature Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is tested by feature analysis — compare each claimed feature against prior art items to see if all features are disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create feature tables to map claim elements to prior art (example provided for a watering device). If any single prior art lacks a claimed feature, novelty may be retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Reports and Applicant Responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners will issue Search Reports and either Adverse or Clear Reports; the applicant has 2 months to submit corrections/arguments (Reg.27C(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare timely and reasoned responses to adverse findings, submit amendments or arguments within the two‑month window to avoid procedural prejudice; be familiar with sample report formats to anticipate examiner concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Granting Procedure Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent granting procedure steps: Filing Application (Form 1/14/2A) → Preliminary Examination (Preliminary Examination Report) → Application Available for Public Inspection (18 months) → Request for Substantive or Modified Substantive Examination (Form 5/5A/5B) → Substantive or Modified Substantive Examination (Search and Examination Report) → Grant or Refusal (Issue Certificate of Grant or Notice of Refusal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sequence and deadlines closely; ensure required forms/fees are filed at each stage and be ready to respond to examination reports to progress toward grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Protection and Term Lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of protection include Patent (an exclusive right granted for inventions) protected 20 years from filing (subject to annual fees) and Utility Innovation (for 'minor' inventions) protected 10 + 5 + 5 years from filing subject to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose between patent and utility innovation routes based on invention maturity and expected term; budget for maintenance/annual fees for patents and ensure use requirements for utility innovations are met.
